title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 29 (Agreements void for uncertainty)

content.overview: Section 29 provides that agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.
content.glance: Agreement whose meaning is not certain or capable of being made certain → void.
content.study: Agreements whose meaning is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void. Terms that can be ascertained by an objective method (e.g. market price, usual course of dealing) are capable of being made certain. Current-law framing: identify the allegedly uncertain term; test whether meaning is certain or can be made certain; conclude voidness only if not.

sections.heading: Uncertainty
sections.body: Agreements the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void.

examples.title: Unidentifiable subject-matter
examples.body: An agreement to sell ‘a hundred tons of oil’ without identifying the kind or source, and with no method of determination, may be void for uncertainty under s. 29.

hypotheticals.question: Is every broadly worded term void under s. 29?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Only if the meaning is not certain and not capable of being made certain.

misconceptions.correction: Section 29 requires that the meaning is not certain or capable of being made certain.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 29 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the term. II. Test certainty or capability of being made certain. III. Conclude voidness only if neither. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Quote ‘certain, or capable of being made certain’.
Give an example of ascertainable price.
